title: Flamenco palmas (rhythmic clapping)
summary: Palmas are the rhythmic hand-claps of flamenco. Two kinds are used: palmas sordas, with cupped hands, give a hollow, soft sound; palmas claras, with the fingers against the palm, give a sharp one. Pitos are finger snaps. Together they hold the compas, the twelve-beat cycle on which the dancing and singing rest.
howToPlay: A wheel of twelve beats turns above the pads; the accents at 3, 6, 8, 10 and 12 are marked in gold.
Four pads are lit: Sorda (soft, cupped), Clara (sharp), Pitos (snaps) and Golpe (a slap on the thigh). A ring closes on a pad when it is time.
Clara on the accents, Sorda on the beats between.
rules: A stroke on the beat is perfect, a near one is good, and extra strokes cost points.
Each pattern is played twice through.
Patterns are simplified teaching figures in the style of the tradition, not transcriptions.
heritageNote: Learning to keep the compas with palmas is the first step of every flamenco musician. The accents fall in a pattern that is felt rather than counted.
